answer: Randomized Adjudication Terrace: each epoch, a verifiable random draw (public seed, no precompute) assigns identities to review cells whose membership is hidden until opened. An attacker needs many concurrent identities to control a cell’s quorum, so each must stay funded and active through the reef of rotating assignments—cost scales with cell size, not one-time registration. Missed participation forfeits a glacier-like slow-decaying deposit, making mass silent sybils expensive.
